slides.title: Exploration vs Exploitation
slides.prompt: What is the role of the epsilon ($ε$) parameter in the $ε$-greedy action selection policy?
options: Balancing random exploratory actions with high-reward exploitative actions
Scaling the learning rate of the neural network optimizer
Discounting future rewards in Bellman equations
Setting the batch size of the experience replay buffer
slides.correctAnswer: Balancing random exploratory actions with high-reward exploitative actions

slides.title: Experience Replay Buffer
slides.prompt: Fill in the component used in Deep Q-Networks (DQN) to break temporal correlation between training samples.

slides.title: Q-Learning Bellman Equation
slides.prompt: What does the discount factor ($γ$) control in the Bellman optimality equation?
options: The relative importance of future rewards compared to immediate rewards
The speed of neural network backpropagation
The size of observation vector arrays
slides.correctAnswer: The relative importance of future rewards compared to immediate rewards

slides.title: Target Network Synchronization
slides.prompt: Fill in the term for updating the target network weights periodically to stabilize DQN training.

slides.title: Policy Gradient vs Q-Learning
slides.prompt: Why are Policy Gradient methods (e.g., PPO) preferred over Deep Q-Networks for continuous action spaces?
options: They directly parameterize continuous probability distributions over action outputs
They do not require GPU hardware acceleration
They eliminate the need for environment states
slides.correctAnswer: They directly parameterize continuous probability distributions over action outputs
